name: West Virginia

events.title: Statehood
events.text: West Virginia became the 35th state on June 20, 1863.

events.title: 1880 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1880 census, West Virginia's House delegation grew from 3 to 4 seats.

events.title: 1890 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1890 census, West Virginia kept 4 seats in the House.

events.title: 1900 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1900 census, West Virginia's House delegation grew from 4 to 5 seats.

events.title: 1910 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1910 census, West Virginia's House delegation grew from 5 to 6 seats.

events.title: Some members elected at-large
events.text: In the 63rd through 64th Congresses (1913–1917), West Virginia elected one of its representatives statewide (at-large) and the rest by district.

events.title: 1930 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1930 census, West Virginia kept 6 seats in the House.

events.title: 1940 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1940 census, West Virginia kept 6 seats in the House.

events.title: 1950 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1950 census, West Virginia kept 6 seats in the House.

events.title: 1960 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1960 census, West Virginia's House delegation shrank from 6 to 5 seats.

events.title: 1970 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1970 census, West Virginia's House delegation shrank from 5 to 4 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1980 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1980 census, West Virginia kept 4 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1990 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1990 census, West Virginia's House delegation shrank from 4 to 3 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 2000 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2000 census, West Virginia kept 3 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Tennant v. Jefferson County Commission
events.text: A federal district court blocked the 2011 congressional map over a 0.79% population variance. On September 25, 2012, the U.S. Supreme Court reversed, finding the variance justified by goals such as keeping counties whole, which West Virginia had never split.

events.title: 2010 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2010 census, West Virginia kept 3 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Two-district map enacted
events.text: After losing a seat in the 2020 census, the legislature passed a two-district plan (SB 3033) on October 15, 2021; the governor signed it on October 22. No court challenge appears to have been filed.

events.title: 2020 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2020 census, West Virginia's House delegation shrank from 3 to 2 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.

c048.text: New map drawn after the 1880 census, which raised West Virginia's seats from 3 to 4. It was first used in the 1882 election.

c058.text: New map drawn after the 1900 census, which raised West Virginia's seats from 4 to 5. It was first used in the 1902 election.

c063.text: After the 1910 census raised West Virginia's seats from 5 to 6, the state kept its existing districts and elected one member statewide (at-large).

c065.text: West Virginia's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1916 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c072.text: West Virginia's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1930 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c074.text: New map drawn after the 1930 census, which left West Virginia with 6 seats. It was first used in the 1934 election.

c083.text: New map drawn after the 1950 census, which left West Virginia with 6 seats. It was first used in the 1952 election.

c088.text: New map drawn after the 1960 census, which cut West Virginia's seats from 6 to 5. It was first used in the 1962 election.

c091.text: West Virginia's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1968 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c093.text: New map drawn after the 1970 census, which cut West Virginia's seats from 5 to 4. It was first used in the 1972 election.

c098.text: New map drawn after the 1980 census, which left West Virginia with 4 seats. It was first used in the 1982 election.

c103.text: New map drawn after the 1990 census, which cut West Virginia's seats from 4 to 3. It was first used in the 1992 election.

c108.text: New map drawn after the 2000 census, which left West Virginia with 3 seats. It was first used in the 2002 election.

c113.text: New map drawn after the 2010 census, which left West Virginia with 3 seats. It was first used in the 2012 election.

c118.text: New map following: Two-district map enacted. After losing a seat in the 2020 census, the legislature passed a two-district plan (SB 3033) on October 15, 2021; the governor signed it on October 22. No court challenge appears to have been filed.
